findings.title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated when the module is imported, not when an `AssignmentSource` is created. Every instance in a long-lived worker therefore gets essentially the same timestamp (process start), so the field is not a real queue time. Any future staleness, ordering, or debugging logic based on it will be wrong. Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead, and have the test assert the value is a recent datetime rather than just non-None.

findings.title: No coverage for deassign loop prevention or cross-integration propagation
findings.body: The new tests cover `assign` when the source integration matches the target, but not the corresponding `deassign` path that was also changed, and they only use a single integration. There is no assertion that an assignment triggered by integration A is still propagated to integration B. A regression that suppresses all outbound syncs whenever a source is present, or that leaves the deassign loop in place, would pass these tests. Add cases with two linked integrations and a matching-source deassign.
